title: An agent with no identity pairs with its person by a spoken code: it asks Lys for the code, the person enters it signed in, names the agent and gives its roots, and Lys certifies the key and tells it which apps to reach
purpose: Tom, 22 Oct 2026 20:1x, typed: "how do people install it for their agents, we need to make that effortless. we'd talked about creating a generic mcp entrypoint so you didnt have to have the details up front. then the ai would connect to their identity or create a new one"; and: "the mcp server still needs to be stdio for claude to receive notifications, just need to make it so you can connect to an identity during runtime". Today an agent gets its identity in one of two ways, both needing details up front on the computer it runs on: `lys agent enrol` (AGENTS-017 R1, R5: commands/enrol.rs) needs a registered agent id and either the registering agent's signature or the responsible person's app pass on that computer; Cambium's `cambium-mcp --take <door_url> <code>` needs the door's address and a take code a person minted by founding the seat first. Neither lets an agent that was just started with nothing say "I have no identity" and get one from the person in front of it. The person's side of founding already exists: the dashboard registers an agent, reviews its profile and gives it roots (AGENTS-017 R4), and /apps lists the organisation's approved apps with their addresses (DIRECTORY-114 R1). What is missing is the pairing: a code the agent can say and the person can type.
task: Add pairing to Lys: an unknown key asks for a pairing code; a signed-in person enters the code, names the agent, gives its roots and approves; Lys certifies the key and answers the agent its identity and the approved apps it may reach. In: the pairing routes and their store, the dashboard's Pair page, the CLI's `lys agent pair` for an agent that is not an MCP seat, the tests. Out: any product's seat server (Cambium's MCP learns the client side in its own brief), a device-code OAuth grant for people, pairing an agent to a person who has no Lys yet (founding an organisation stays the founding path of DIRECTORY-111; the Pair page sends a stranger there and back).

requirements.title: An unknown key asks for a pairing code and waits for the person's decision without polling
requirements.spec: WHEN a caller with no identity POSTs /pair with a PKCS#10 request over a fresh key and the name it proposes THE SYSTEM SHALL answer a pairing code of four lowercase dictionary words (from the word list lys-core already holds for handed links, or one added beside it), a wait id, and the address to tell the person (<lys origin>/pair). THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the request, keyed by the code, until it is decided; a code is never reused while it is undecided. WHEN the caller GETs /pair/{wait} THE SYSTEM SHALL hold the request open until the pairing is decided and then answer it (R3), or refuse at once by name if the wait id is unknown or already answered; no poll interval and no fixed deadline is written anywhere (Tom: no fixed waits, ever); the holding is the server's own event. A pairing the person has not decided is listed on the person's dashboard until they decide it; nothing expires it by a timer.
acceptance: crates/lys-identity-server/src/pair_tests.rs: POST /pair with a valid request answers four words, a wait id and the pair address; a second POST answers a different code; GET /pair/{wait} on an undecided pairing does not answer until a decision is written, then answers it (proved with the server's own notification, no sleep); an unknown wait id is refused pair_unknown.
crates/lys-identity-server/src/pair_tests.rs: a request that is not a valid PKCS#10 over an Ed25519 key is refused pair_request_invalid before anything is kept.

requirements.title: A signed-in person enters the code, names the agent, gives its roots and approves, on one page
requirements.spec: WHEN a signed-in person opens /pair THE SYSTEM SHALL show one field for the four words and, once a code matches an undecided pairing, the agent's proposed name (editable), the roots choice AGENTS-017 R4 already draws, and Approve and Decline. WHEN the person approves THE SYSTEM SHALL register the agent under that person exactly as the dashboard's register act does (the same route, the same review of the reviewed profile if one is named, the same grant of roots), certify the pairing's key through the same path POST /agents/{id}/certificates uses, and record the decision so R1's wait answers. WHEN the person declines THE SYSTEM SHALL record the decline so the wait answers pair_declined and keeps nothing of the key. A stranger who opens /pair is sent to sign in or to found an organisation (DIRECTORY-111) and returns to /pair with the code kept in the page's state, never in the URL.
acceptance: surface/identity/src/features/pair/pair-page.test.tsx: entering a known code shows the proposed name and the roots choice; Approve posts to /pair/{code}/approve with the name and roots and shows 'Paired: <name> can now act as itself'; Decline posts to /pair/{code}/decline; an unknown code shows 'No agent is waiting with these words'.

crates/lys-identity-server/src/pair_tests.rs: approve registers the agent under the signed-in person, issues a certificate with a serial in the log, and the held GET /pair/{wait} answers the certificate, the agent id and the person's handle; decline answers pair_declined and the key is not kept; a person who is not signed in is refused on both.
A code kept in the page's state survives the sign-in round trip (test with the sign-in return path).

requirements.title: The answer tells the agent who it is and which approved apps it may reach
requirements.spec: WHEN a pairing is approved THE SYSTEM SHALL answer the waiting agent: its agent id, its handle, the certificate PEM and serial, the Lys API address, the responsible person's handle, and the organisation's approved apps as /apps answers them (DIRECTORY-114: id, name, address) so the agent can reach each product's door without being told any address up front. The answer carries no key material of anyone else and no secret the agent did not make.
acceptance: crates/lys-identity-server/src/pair_tests.rs: with two approved apps and one pending, the answer lists the two approved with their addresses and not the pending one; the certificate verifies against the issuer; the serial is in the log.

requirements.title: `lys agent pair` does the agent's side for an agent that is not a product seat
requirements.spec: WHEN `lys agent pair --lys <api> --name <name> --seat <path>` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL make the key where it runs (as enrol does), POST /pair, print the four words and the address for the person, hold GET /pair/{wait} until it answers, and write the seat file (lys_core::seat_file, 0600, never overwriting) with the certificate, serial, agent id and Lys address; a decline is printed by name and nothing is written. The printed words are the only thing the person needs to hear.
acceptance: crates/lys/src/commands/pair_tests.rs: against a test server the command prints the four words, writes the seat file after approval, and refuses seat_file_exists before making a key when the path exists; a decline prints pair_declined and writes nothing.

boundaries: No product's name or address is written into Lys outside tests and fixtures (the no-app-names rule stands); the apps answered come from /apps as the organisation approved them.
No sleep, timeout, poll interval or expiry timer: the wait is held by the server's own event, and an undecided pairing stays listed until a person decides it.
No pairing without a signed-in person: a code alone never registers, certifies or reaches anything; a stranger is sent to sign in or found, and back.
Nothing changes in enrol, in certificates for already-registered agents, or in any product's seat server; every file stays under 500 lines of code.
verification: Red first: every new test written and shown red at the brief commit through `cargo nextest run -p lys-identity-server -p lys -E 'test(pair)'` and the identity surface's vitest on pair-page.test.tsx, on Dean's laptop, green at the fix commit, judged by the runs' output lines and never by an exit code.
The whole gate (tokei, ast-grep, fmt, clippy pedantic, nextest, cargo test --doc, tsc, vitest) at the landing sha, judged by its output.

Walked on the install with Tom: `lys agent pair` on this laptop says four words, Tom types them on his dashboard, names the agent and approves, and the command writes the seat file and prints the agent's id; then Cambium's seat brief walks the same code from an MCP seat.

Hospital line in the handback, never in a commit: if this code were used in a hospital, the worst credible failure is a pairing approved for the wrong agent because two agents asked at once and the words were confused, so a stranger's agent acts as the ward's, and it could harm about everyone that agent may reach.

amendments.subject: R1's file list: the word list, the state, the router and the tables
amendments.ruling: lys-core holds no word list for handed links (DIRECTORY-112's handed link is a token a person clicks), so the brief's "one added beside it" is crates/lys-core/src/pairing_words.rs, exported from lys-core's lib.rs: two hundred and fifty-six common short English words, no two alike aloud and none with a spelling variant a listener might type (Tom's ruling of 23 Oct), one per byte, so four bytes from the operating system make a code. The store is a field of AppState (routes.rs: `pairings: Mutex<PairStore>`), opened beside foundings.json as pairings.json with no new configuration key, so routes_startup.rs, grant_settlement_seed_tests.rs and tests/budgets_feed_entries.rs set it; routes_table.rs merges the pair routes; openapi_table.rs and openapi_types.rs carry the two routes' rows, since tests/openapi.rs refuses any declared route without an entry; error_status.rs maps pair_unknown to 404 and pair_request_invalid to 400 (pair_declined keeps the named refusal's 409); certificates_issue.rs opens request_der to the crate so the pairing reads a request exactly as the certificate route does. The pairings file is written whole as one durable operation per ask, decision or taken answer, the shape foundings.json uses, never leaf by leaf.

amendments.subject: R2, R3, R4 as built
amendments.ruling: The person's routes are GET /pair/{code}/waiting (the agent waiting with these words), POST /pair/{code}/approve and POST /pair/{code}/decline, all for a signed-in person; the agent's GET /pair/{wait} stands. The approve body carries the registration's operation, an activate operation, a certificate operation (the serial) and the display name, plus the roots as the dashboard's register act makes them (operation, source grant, resource, relation, window), so nothing is derived from another id and a retry carries the same ids. Lys keeps no handles: the answer's handle is the name the person gave the agent and person is the responsible person's display name. The Pair page keeps the typed words in this tab's sessionStorage (lys.pair.code), never in the address, and looks them up again on return from sign-in. The CLI is lys agent pair --lys <api> --name <name> --seat <path>; it prints the words and the address the moment Lys gives them (one JSON line in --json mode) and the seat file's path, agent, serial and apps at the end.

amendments.subject: R2's file list grows by the certificate path, found at the first build
amendments.ruling: A pairing's PKCS#10 request is made before the agent has an id, under the name it proposed, and lys-core's authority refuses a request whose common name is not the subject issued for. R2 therefore adds CertificateAuthority::issue_certificate_for_pairing in crates/lys-core/src/ca/authority.rs (the request's common name must equal the proposed name kept at the ask, so the one request the person approved is certified and no other; the subject is the agent id Lys gave) and certificates_issue::issued_for_pairing in crates/lys-identity-server/src/certificates_issue.rs, the same claims, signing key and log entry as POST /agents/{id}/certificates. The decision routes live in crates/lys-identity-server/src/pair_decide.rs beside pair.rs, with their rows in openapi_table.rs and openapi_types.rs. Enrol and every certificate of an already registered agent are unchanged.

amendments.subject: The three deciding routes are a person's alone; decline takes no body
amendments.ruling: GET /pair/{code}/waiting, POST /pair/{code}/approve and POST /pair/{code}/decline sit on HUMAN_ONLY (openapi_table.rs) with the reason PAIRING: a pairing is a person's to decide, since approval registers the agent under the signed-in person, who answers for it; an agent calling any of the three is refused with that reason, as it is for an access request's approve and decline (AGENTS-019). POST /pair/{code}/decline takes no body, the four words being in the path, so it is listed on NO_BODY (tests/shared/openapi_unnamed.rs). The surface's required-field contract (surface/identity/tests/server-required-fields.json) names POST /pair/{code}/approve with activate, certificate, display_name and operation; grants defaults to none. The approve row's unavailable-apps refusal is apps_unavailable, the name the apps store produces; AppsUnavailable was never produced and is gone from the row.

amendments.subject: A cut hold is held again; the answer is read until the agent says it has it
amendments.ruling: Live run at ec213e48 over https://lys.ablative.com.au/api: the agent was told its words and held GET /pair/{wait}; Cloudflare cut the held request at its own limit (about 100 s) with 524 and no JSON, and lys agent pair gave up (pair_answer_unreadable). Two changes. (1) The CLI holds again at once on the event that the hold was cut: the connection closed with no whole answer (the transport's Uncertain), or a 5xx with no JSON, which is a proxy's word and never Lys's; it stops only on Lys's JSON (an answer or a refusal). No clock anywhere. (2) GET /pair/{wait} reads the decision and consumes nothing (pair_store decided), so a hold cut after the decision, or a handler not cancelled by a closed socket, can never spend the answer into a dead connection; the agent says it has its answer with POST /pair/{wait}/taken (public, the wait id being the agent's own secret), which removes the decided pairing durably, once; an undecided, unknown or taken wait is pair_unknown. The CLI posts taken after the seat file is written, and before it answers a decline, so nothing of a decided pairing stays in Lys; a refusal of the take is printed and changes nothing. Tests: the server test reads the same decline twice, takes it, and finds the wait gone; the CLI test runs the command through a loopback proxy that answers the first hold 524 with no body and carries every other exchange whole, and sees two holds and one take. R2's file list grows by pair_tests.rs and tests/shared/openapi_unnamed.rs; R4's by nothing new.

amendments.subject: A planned Lys restart sends the hold away; it is taken up again at the instant Lys announces
amendments.ruling: Upgrading the installed Lys to 8531b41c answered the proof agent's held GET /pair/{wait} with 503 LysGoingAway (planned_stop.rs frames every held GET so), and lys agent pair treated that JSON refusal as final and stopped, although the pairing is durable and Lys was back within its announced return. The CLI now does what the runner does on the same frame (dial/bridge.rs resume_at): it reads expected_return, the instant Lys itself names, says so, holds again at that instant, and never on a clock of its own; a frame with no expected_return is pair_answer_unreadable. Lys unreachable at the instant it announced is refused lys_not_returned, naming the instant and that the pairing is kept by Lys, so a Lys that misses its own announcement is a loud, named failure and never a silent spin; over a proxy, a down Lys is the proxy's 5xx with no JSON, already held again on that event. Tests: the loopback proxy answers the first hold as Lys going away now, and the pairing completes with the hold taken up again; the proxy that stops listening after that frame makes the command refuse lys_not_returned, with one hold and no seat file.
